ruling.recommended_action: Refund the $6.61 cancellation fee to the rider as a Ryde voucher (NS-7) and send the driver's account to Ryde review for the false arrival confirmation; + flag_account
ruling.reasoning:
The cancellation fee stands only through NS-0's driver-cancellation branch: the driver cancelled at 12:09:25 (7 min 25 s after acceptance) and asserted the rider was a no-show, which puts the case under NS-1/NS-2 [F3][NS-0]. Cancelled_by = driver and the driver's own statement claims non-appearance, so the fee's validity turns on NS-1's three conditions [F12][NS-1].

NS-1 (i) is met but (ii) fails. The driver tapped "I'm Here" at 12:06:15, so an arrival was confirmed by driver_tap [F5][NS-1]. But at that moment the GPS put him 600 m from the pickup point, and his closest approach for the whole trip was 599 m — he was never inside the 200 m zone [F5][F1]. NS-1 (ii) requires the tap to be made while GPS shows the driver at the pickup location; it is therefore not satisfied [NS-1].

NS-1 (iii) fails as well. After the tap at 12:06:15 the driver spent 0 s continuously within 200 m of the pickup, and the trace shows samples run without a gap to the cancellation, so the record settles the point rather than leaving it undetermined [F5][NS-1]. His 3 min 30 s stationary period (12:05:55–12:09:25) was clocked at 600 m from the pickup — the trace computed (1.3048, 103.8549) as 600 m away — so the wait occurred outside the zone and time waited elsewhere does not count [F2][F5][NS-1].

The platform record is consistent: driver_arrived_at is null, so the only arrival signal in the file is the driver's own button press made 600 m away [F4][F5][NS-1]. Where the driver's post-trip statement says he "waited more than 3 minutes at the pickup", it is contradicted by the system records at F1, F2 and F5, and system records override statements, so the statement is not relied on [F12][F2][F5][NS-1]. The chats fit the same picture: the driver wrote at 12:06 "I'm here already, silver Toyota Altis, please come out" while 600 m away, and the rider replied at 12:07 "I'm at the pickup point, no car here. Where are you?", with the driver cancelling at 12:09 [F8][F9][F10][F1]. Traffic and weather (band 3 on Jalan Besar, no incidents, fair weather) provide no "reasonable cause" narrative here and are not relied on by either side [F13][F14][F15][RD-4].

Because at least one NS-1 condition fails, NS-2 applies: the $6.61 cancellation fee must be refunded in full to the rider [F3][F6][NS-1][NS-2]. The fee on record is exactly $6.61, so the refund is the full disputed item, not a computed per-km amount [F3][F6][NS-2]. Refund form follows NS-7: a Ryde voucher, not cash, and the dispute is timely, filed on the same record as the 12:09:25 cancellation, well inside the 30-day window [F3][F6][NS-7]. Separately, the trace confirms the driver confirmed arrival while not at the pickup (600 m at the moment of tap, closest approach 599 m), which is the abuse-of-the-arrival-button situation NS-2 attaches an account flag to [F5][F1][NS-2]; the driver concedes the factual basis, and a flag is an added action, not the basis of the finding [F17][NS-2].

On safety: I read the complaint, the full 3-message timestamped chat and the driver's statement [F11][F8][F9][F10]. The messages are confined to pickup location, a vehicle description and the driver's decision to cancel; the complaint concerns being charged a no-show fee [F8][F9][F10][F12]. There is no threat, intimidation, harassment, sexual remark or dangerous-driving allegation, so the screen is "none" and no escalation under SAFE-1 or SAFE-2 is triggered [F8][F9][F10][F12][SAFE-1][SAFE-2]. Evidence is sufficient: the GPS trace covers the wait to cancellation without a hole, the arrival tap and its distance are recorded, and the fare record shows the exact fee, so no element of the ruling is left unsettled [F1][F4][F5][F6][NS-1][NS-2].

rejected_claims.reason: The claim's underlying point (the statement is overridden) is accepted, but the rider's framing that F12 is simply 'not relied on' is only partly right: F12 is contradicted by F1, F2 and F5, and system records win over statements, so the statement's location claim fails [F12][F2][F5][NS-1]. No separate relief flows from this claim beyond the refund already ordered.

The driver's 90-day record (1 dispute, 1 upheld, no-show: 1) is a profile fact that may support an added account-review flag but cannot decide the case or amount on its own [F17][RD-6]. The flag here rests on the false arrival confirmation at F5/F1 under NS-2, not on the profile.

The driver's longevity profile (6.3-year account, 4.67 rating, 464 trips in 90 days) does not excuse a tap made 600 m from the pickup; profile facts never decide a case alone, and the abuse-of-arrival-button condition in NS-2 is met by F5 and F1 regardless of account history [F5][F17][NS-2].

Timeliness under NS-7 is accepted as far as the record goes, but no separate amount follows from it: the refund quantum comes from the fee on record at F3/F6 under NS-2, with NS-7 only fixing the voucher form [F3][F6][NS-2][NS-7].
